chunks: Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarood, who said: He said to me, Abu Ja'far:
This matter (of the Imamate/Leadership) will not occur except in the one of us who is the most obscure in memory (knowledge) and the youngest in age.

key_terms.أَخْمَلِنَا ذِكْرًا: The most obscure in memory/knowledge (least known)
key_terms.الْأَمْرَ: The matter/authority (referring to Imamate or leadership)

ai.seo_question: Who is the Imam according to the hadith of being the youngest and most obscure?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) identifies the criteria for the Mahdi as being 'least known' (akhmal) and 'youngest' (ahdath), which Shia scholars interpret as the signs of the Major Occultation where the Imam remains hidden from public view to avoid premature detection by enemies. This narration underscores the theological concept of *ghaybah* as a divine protection and a test of faith, distinguishing the Mahdi's status from previous prophets who were openly recognized.
